seo.title: How Much Does a Startup Rebrand Cost?
seo.description: Startup rebrand cost: $3,000–$10,000 with a senior freelancer or sprint, $10,000–$25,000 with a studio, $60,000+ with an agency, plus the rollout costs to plan for.

body:
A startup rebrand costs about $3,000 to $10,000 with a senior freelancer or a one-week brand sprint, $10,000 to $25,000 with an independent studio and $60,000 or more with an agency.

On top of the new identity, budget for the rollout: your website, pitch deck, product and social accounts all need to change too.

The identity ranges come from 11 published brand identity packages I checked for my guide to what a complete brand identity costs.

Disclosure: I sell one of those options, a one-week Brand Sprint for $3,000, so I show it in the same table as everyone else.

What does a startup rebrand include?

A rebrand has two parts, and most quotes only cover the first one.

The identity is the logo, colours, typography, brand guidelines and the core assets your team uses every day.

The rollout is everything that has to change afterwards: the website, pitch deck, product UI, social profiles, email templates and any printed or physical pieces.

A seed-stage startup usually needs both within a few weeks, because investors and customers see the website and deck before anything else.

Startup rebrand cost by who you hire

The provider you choose changes the price more than the size of your company.

What else does a rebrand cost?

The identity is often the smaller part of the total, so plan the rollout before you sign anything.

Website: new brand colours and type on an old site rarely look right, so most startups redesign at least the homepage and key pages.

Pitch deck and sales materials: the deck is usually the first thing investors see with the new brand.

Product UI and app icons: your product should match the new identity, which means design and engineering time.

Trademark search and filing: check the new name or mark with a trademark attorney before launch.

Swag, signage and print: only if you have an office, events or physical products.

Your team's time: someone has to update profiles, templates and tools, which is easy to forget in the budget.

What did my startup rebrands cost?

These are real projects from my case studies, priced at my current flat rate of $3,000 per week.

Some of these projects were priced differently at the time, so read the last column as what the same scope costs today.

NextDim went on to secure $2.5M in seed funding and Orbio $1.2M after their rebrands.

Who does fast, senior-led startup rebrands?

A rebrand can be fast without being cheap work, as long as the scope is fixed and a senior designer does it.

One-week brand sprints deliver the core identity in five working days, then add website and deck weeks if you need them.

Senior freelancers usually need four to six weeks, because they fit your project around other clients.

Sprint-style agencies can also move in two weeks, but at agency prices.

Whoever you choose, ask who does the work, how many concepts you will see and whether the price is fixed, as in my list of questions to ask before hiring a brand designer.

How long does a startup rebrand take?

The identity takes one week in a sprint, and four to six weeks with most freelancers.

A website adds two to four weeks: a week of design, then one or two of development.

Agencies usually take three to nine months, mostly because of research phases and stakeholder reviews.

For the week-by-week breakdown, read how long branding takes.

When is a startup rebrand worth the money?

A rebrand pays off when the brand is actively costing you trust, deals or hires.

Before a raise: investors judge the deck and website in minutes, as I explain in why you need branding before you raise.

After a pivot: when the product or audience has changed, the old brand describes a company you no longer are.

When you have outgrown an MVP logo: a logo made in a weekend often breaks down at sales, enterprise or hiring stage.

It is not worth it when you have no product-market fit yet, or when the real problem is messaging rather than design.

How to budget for a startup rebrand

Start with the date you need it by, then work backwards.

  • Decide what must be ready on launch day: identity only, or identity, website and deck.
  • Get two or three quotes with the same scope, and compare them line by line.
  • Add the rollout: website, deck, product UI, social and legal checks.
  • Name one decision-maker, so feedback does not stall the project.
  • Keep 10 to 20% aside for things you will only notice after launch.

If you want the identity in a week, see the Brand Sprint or my pricing.

faq.question: How much does a startup rebrand cost?
faq.answer: In the published packages I checked, a startup rebrand identity costs about $2,500 to $10,000 with a senior freelancer, $3,000 for a one-week brand sprint, $10,000 to $25,000 with an independent studio and $60,000 or more with an agency. Budget extra for the website, pitch deck and product updates.

faq.question: How long does a startup rebrand take?
faq.answer: One week for the core identity in a brand sprint, four to six weeks with most freelancers, and three to nine months with an agency. A website adds two to four weeks.

faq.question: What does a rebrand include?
faq.answer: The identity: logo, colours, typography, guidelines and core assets. The rollout then updates the website, pitch deck, product UI, social profiles and any printed or physical pieces.

faq.question: Is a cheap rebrand worth it?
faq.answer: Rarely. A few-hundred-dollar logo is not a brand system. Compare what the guidelines include, how many concepts you get and who actually does the work.

faq.question: Should a startup rebrand before fundraising?
faq.answer: Often, yes, if the current brand makes the company look smaller or less credible than it is. Investors see the deck and website first, and a one-week rebrand fits most raise timelines.
